headline: FURY GOLD DRILLS 9.81 G/T AU IN 7 ZONES AT EAU CLAIRE — Phase 2 Resource Conversion Advances James Bay Quebec Flagship Deposit
snippet: Fury Gold Mines released new drill assays from five holes at the Eau Claire deposit in James Bay, Quebec, confirming gold mineralization across seven distinct zones with a peak intercept of 9.81 g/t Au over 2.99 metres. The results are part of a Phase 2 resource conversion program designed to upgrade existing inferred resources to higher confidence categories ahead of a feasibility study. Eau Claire is one of the largest undeveloped gold deposits in James Bay and is drawing significant attention from senior producers as the district's infrastructure improves.

headline: ALAMOS GOLD TAKES 14.9% OF TRIDENT RESOURCES FOR C$25.9M — Major Miner's Strategic Bet Signals Confidence in Junior's Project Pipeline
snippet: Alamos Gold (TSX/NYSE: AGI) agreed to acquire approximately 7,420,000 shares of Trident Resources in a private placement for C$25.9 million, giving the mid-tier gold producer a 14.9% stake expected to close in December 2026. The investment follows Alamos's established pattern of taking minority positions in junior developers to secure optionality before committing to full acquisition — a strategy it used with Island Gold before that mine became one of Canada's lowest-cost operations. For Trident shareholders, a 14.9% Alamos position is both a de-risking signal and a potential take-out premium.

headline: CONGO BANS ALL COBALT EXPORTS FROM NOVEMBER 30 — ARECOMS Halts Shipments Indefinitely; 70% of Global Supply Goes Offline
snippet: The DRC's strategic minerals regulator ARECOMS announced it will suspend all cobalt exports — from industrial mines and artisanal operations alike — from November 30, 2026 until further notice, citing a "significant and sustained decline" in prices due to chronic oversupply. No fixed end date was set; a quota review is planned in approximately four months. The DRC produces over 70% of global cobalt supply, and the full suspension replaces the existing 96,600-tonne annual quota system. Battery cathode manufacturers in China and South Korea who depend on DRC hydroxide will face immediate supply chain disruption.

headline: SILVER BREAKS DOWN 2.93% TO $41.85 — Gold/Silver Ratio Widens to 86.45 as Industrial Metal Selloff Weighs on White Metal
snippet: Silver fell 2.93% to $41.85 per troy ounce on November 24, underperforming gold's modest recovery and widening the gold/silver ratio to 86.45 from 84.32 the prior session — an extreme historical discount for silver relative to gold. The divergence reflects silver's dual role: safe-haven demand is supportive, but the industrial component is being dragged by copper's pullback. At $41.85, silver trades 60% below its 2026 high near $104, leaving high-grade primary silver miners at valuations that have historically preceded multi-year re-ratings.

headline: COPPER RETREATS 2.28% TO $12,205/T — LME Gives Back Nvidia-Driven Gains; Lead Hits 4-Year Low as Industrial Metals Fade
snippet: LME copper fell 2.28% to $12,205 per tonne on November 24 as markets gave back part of Monday's Nvidia-fuelled recovery, with lead simultaneously hitting a four-year low in the same session. The retreat confirms Monday's bounce was sentiment-driven rather than fundamental: physical copper demand from Chinese smelters remained robust throughout the selloff — buyers continued paying record import premiums of $360-500/tonne — but paper market positioning remains net-short and prone to momentum reversals. Copper is down approximately 17% from its September record of $14,694/tonne.

headline: PROSPECTIVA DRILLS 10.02M AT 11.75% COPPER IN BRAZIL MAIDEN HOLE — São Francisco Returns Highest-Grade Intersection in Company History
snippet: Prospectiva Resources (TSX-V: PSVA) reported 10.02 metres grading 11.75% copper with 0.87 g/t gold and 1.09% zinc from its maiden drill program at the São Francisco project in Brazil — described as the highest-grade copper intersection in the company's history. High-sulphide copper grades above 10% are rare in modern exploration and suggest a potentially economic near-surface massive sulphide deposit. With copper at $5.56/lb and AI datacenter demand driving long-term bullish fundamentals, an 11.75% Cu intercept in a known Brazilian copper district is the kind of maiden result that attracts follow-up capital.

headline: GALLEON GOLD DRILLS 3.01 G/T AU OVER 7M — West Cache Zone #9 Now Extends 590M Vertical, Open at Depth; Ontario Target Deepens
snippet: Galleon Gold (TSX-V: GGO) extended Zone #9 at its West Cache property in Ontario to more than 590 metres of vertical extent, with hole WC-26-253 intersecting 3.01 g/t Au over 7.00 metres 80 metres down-dip of previous drilling — with the zone remaining open at depth. A structurally-controlled gold system extending beyond 590 metres vertically without reaching its bottom suggests Zone #9 carries meaningful resource depth that the current estimate does not yet capture. Ontario's west-central gold corridor has drawn increasing senior miner attention in 2026.

headline: UBS AND GOLDMAN SACHS SEE GOLD RECOVERING BY LATE 2027 — Both Banks Warn Q4 2026 Average Price Is Key Swing Factor for Mining Equities
snippet: Kitco's weekly Gold SWOT analysis covers UBS and Goldman Sachs both forecasting a gold price recovery through 2027, with central bank accumulation identified as the structural floor under prices. Both banks flag Q4 2026 quarterly average gold price as the pivotal swing factor: if gold averages below $3,500 in Q4, it marks the first negative-average quarter since Q4 2022 and would trigger model-driven selling by systematic funds that have kept positions through the correction. The piece distinguishes speculative selling from the fundamental case, noting sovereign buyers accelerated purchases as prices broke below $4,000.

headline: SCOTTIE RESOURCES TARGETS 2028 PRODUCTION AT SCOTTIE BC MINE — PEA Models 65,000 oz/Year; Feasibility Study Set for Spring 2027
snippet: Scottie Resources (TSX-V: SCOT) outlined its path to production in a Kitco interview, with a preliminary economic assessment modelling approximately 65,000 ounces of annual gold production over a seven-year initial mine life at the Scottie Gold Mine in British Columbia's Golden Triangle, with potential to extend toward ten years. A feasibility study is planned for spring 2027 following more than 61,000 metres of drilling in 2026 — the company's largest program to date. With Golden Triangle road access and existing permits, Scottie's PEA-to-feasibility timeline is among the more credible in the junior sector at current gold prices.

headline: SIRIOS RESOURCES COMMISSIONS CHEECHOO GOLD PEA — James Bay Quebec's Largest Undeveloped Gold Deposit Advances Toward Economic Study
snippet: Sirios Resources selected Synectiq Inc. as lead consultant to complete the Preliminary Economic Assessment of its Cheechoo Gold Project in James Bay, Quebec, marking a critical milestone for one of the largest undeveloped gold deposits in the emerging district. Synectiq will integrate geological, engineering and financial components across the PEA, which will form the basis for further permitting and financing decisions. With Fury Gold also reporting Eau Claire drill results today, the James Bay district is now seeing simultaneous PEA-stage advancement at two of its largest undeveloped gold systems.
